title: Coding agents help scientific teams modernise fragile research software
friendlyTitle: Coding agents are helping scientists repair old software
summary: An OpenAI field report covers eight scientific-computing projects that used Codex, or Codex with Claude Code, for maintenance, optimisation, migrations and redesigns. Teams reported faster engineering work, while scientific validity, edge cases and long-term stewardship remained human responsibilities.
friendlySummary: Eight science projects used coding agents to update, speed up or rebuild research tools. The agents worked quickly, but people still had to check the science and difficult details.
whyItMatters: Researchers can use coding agents to tackle maintenance that would otherwise delay experiments, but speed moves the bottleneck to verification. Measurable acceptance tests, staged changes and a clear maintainer are more important than generating a quick rewrite.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Scientists may spend less time fixing code and more time on research. Good tests and a person responsible for the software are still essential.
